subject: Chemistry
title: Distillation: Alchemy's Greatest Tool
description: A quick, practical guide to Distillation: Alchemy's Greatest Tool.

hook.text: Distillation separates liquids by boiling point. It gave alchemists pure acids, alcohols, and essential oils.

buildup.text: An alembic heats a liquid until it vaporizes. The vapor travels through a cooled tube and condenses as a purer liquid.

discovery.text: Islamic alchemists perfected this technique. The word 'alcohol' comes from Arabic 'al-kuhl'—a distilled substance.

twist.text: Distillation let them isolate nitric acid, sulfuric acid, and ethanol—three reagents that revolutionized chemistry.

climax.text: Today, distillation refines crude oil into gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. The same principle, industrial scale.

punchline.text: Heat, evaporate, condense. One technique that powers chemistry and industry.

quiz.question: What Arabic word is the origin of 'alcohol'?

details.summary: Distillation, alchemy's most important technique, separates substances based on differences in boiling points by vaporizing a liquid and then condensing the vapor..
details.whyItMatters: Distillation remains one of the most fundamental separation techniques in chemistry and industry. Petroleum refining, water purification, beverage production, and pharmaceutical manufacturing all depend on distillation.
takeaways: Distillation exploits boiling point differences to separate substances
The alembic still was perfected by Islamic alchemists for precise separation
Modern industry still relies on distillation for petroleum and chemical refining

faq.question: How did the development of distillation advance chemical knowledge?
faq.answer: Distillation allowed alchemists to isolate pure substances from mixtures for the first time. This enabled discovery of mineral acids, alcohols, and essential oils that could not be obtained otherwise. Pure substances behave predictably, making systematic study possible.

faq.question: What is the difference between simple and fractional distillation?
faq.answer: Simple distillation separates substances with large boiling point differences in one pass. Fractional distillation uses a column packed with material that creates many condensation-evaporation cycles, enabling separation of substances with similar boiling points, as in petroleum refining.
